text:
The Rangers are 9-7-1, 4-5-1 over their last ten, and it would be easy to call it a slump. The chances say otherwise. New York has 52.5% of the expected goals and creates 3.3 per hour, but has scored about five fewer goals than those chances usually bring. Our model counts their 19 points as almost exactly earned, which says the team is a touch better than average and hasn't caught many breaks up front.

Igor Shesterkin is doing his part: .926 and 4.0 goals saved above expected over his last four starts, 3-1-0. The top line of Mika Zibanejad, Alexis Lafrenière and Gabe Perreault has played the most minutes (140) at 59% of the chances and outscored teams 6-3. J.T. Miller with Pavel Dorofeyev and Tye Kartye has been the best by process, 64% and 3.77 expected goals per hour, but it's been outscored 5-4.

The trouble is the middle of the lineup. The Eeli Tolvanen, Will Cuylle and Noah Laba line sits at 46%, and Marcus Pettersson with Sean Durzi is at 45%. Adam Fox and Vladislav Gavrikov carry a heavy 241 minutes and have been on for 13 goals for and 12 against. The power play is modest at 0.66 expected goals a game.

Mike Sullivan's team is a coin flip for the playoffs (48%) on a 92-point pace. The underlying numbers argue for patience.
headline: The Rangers' process is better than their record
